d.d: Alternative spelling of gaff (“place of residence, house”).
A tool consisting of a large metal hook with a handle or pole, especially the one used to pull large fish aboard a boat.
A minor error or faux pas, a gaffe.

d.x: The sideshow feat was just a gaff, but the audience was too proud to admit they'd been fooled.

d.d: To use a gaff, especially to land a fish.
To doctor or modify for deceptive purposes.
A foolish and embarrassing error, especially one made in public; a social blunder; a breach of etiquette.
A chief lighting technician for a motion-picture or television production.
Someone aboard a boat whose duty is to gaff a (large) fish once the angler has reeled it in.
